properties.name: The three-legs audit, finally run over the surface
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-26, answering Anthony's question — *"I believe there are '3 legs' that certain skills need — have they been applied to all skills uniformly?"* The audit had never been run. It has now, over the WHOLE declared vocabulary rather than the three items `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` sampled.

SCOPE: all 64 edge types + 29 node types the schema declares = 93. For each, the three legs — (1) a TYPED TOOL that writes it, (2) an INSTRUCTION in a served skill or tool description saying WHEN, (3) a DETECTOR that notices its ABSENCE.

═══ THE ANSWER: NO, NOT UNIFORMLY ═══

  all three legs      54  (58%)
  tool + instruction  8   (no detector)
  instruction + detector 7 (no tool)
  tool only           7
  tool + detector     1
  instruction only    2
  detector only       1
  ⭐ NO LEGS AT ALL   13  (14%)

═══ 🛑 THE SHARPEST FINDING: FIVE TYPES EXIST ONLY IN THE SCHEMA ═══

`COMPLIES_WITH`, `IMPOSES`, `OPERATES_IN`, `SUPPLEMENTS`, `VIOLATES_RULE` are declared in the schema and appear in ZERO Rust source files, ZERO served skills, and ZERO tool descriptions. Nothing writes them, nothing instructs them, nothing detects them, and no code even names them. `OPERATES_IN` nevertheless has 3 edges in reflow2's own graph — written through raw `create_edge`, which is precisely the escape hatch the three-legs rule says must not count as reachability.

The other eight leg-less types: `ANNOTATES` (11 edges), `ASSESSED_ON`, `CONTAINS_EPOCH`, `EnvironmentRule`, `HAS_SNAPSHOT` (188 edges), `OBSERVED_IN`, `OCCURS_DURING`, `QualityGate`. ALL THIRTEEN share one property: **zero mentions in the MCP layer, zero in any served skill, zero in any tool description.** An agent working a user's project cannot learn these exist by any route reflow2 offers.

⭐ `HAS_SNAPSHOT` IS THE INSTRUCTIVE ONE. It carries 188 edges here, so it plainly WORKS — `record_change` writes it internally. But no skill and no tool description ever names it, so leg 1 is satisfied only by accident of another tool's implementation, and legs 2 and 3 are genuinely absent. Vocabulary can be heavily used and still be unreachable BY INTENT.

═══ THE DECOMPOSES PATTERN, CONFIRMED AND NOT ALONE ═══

Five types have ALL THREE LEGS and zero instances here: `CLAIMS`, `DECOMPOSES`, `DUPLICATES`, `MASKS`, `PRODUCES`. `DECOMPOSES` was the case that first exposed the hidden qualifier on leg 3 — a detector that checks the consistency of what EXISTS cannot ask why none exists — and the audit finds four siblings. This is direct evidence for the FOURTH-LEG hypothesis in `dec:idea-have-the-three-legs-been-applied-uniformly-and-are-three-legs-enough`: three legs present, practice still absent.

═══ ⚠️ HONEST LIMITS, AND THE FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG ═══

THIS IS A MECHANICAL PROXY. A mention is not an instruction and a reference is not an absence-detector, so every YES is an UPPER BOUND: real coverage can only be worse than 58%, never better.

THE FIRST RUN PRODUCED JUNK AND WAS DISCARDED. v1 matched case-sensitively (so `DECOMPOSES` in detect.rs was missed and it reported no detector, contradicting a recorded fact) and derived leg 1 from the type NAME (so `ALLOCATED_TO` read as having no tool, when `allocate` writes it). Both bugs inflated the failure count. v2 resolves leg 1 through the core methods a served tool actually calls, and counts a tool whose DESCRIPTION enumerates the type — `review_relations` names thirteen inference relations that way, and without that rule they read as unreachable when they are not.

THE 13 LEG-LESS TYPES WERE HAND-VERIFIED against the whole repo rather than trusted from the proxy. The 54 were not.

📌 `vocabulary_coverage` was checked FIRST, per the option (b) instruction to look before building. It answers a DIFFERENT question — which vocabulary ONE DESIGN has used (43/64 edge types, 23/29 node types here) — and is per-design, not per-surface. It is nevertheless a partial answer to leg 3's hidden qualifier: it is the one computation that asks 'you have never used this at all', which `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs` said nothing did.
